drivingQuestion: From where do we know one is liable for an intentional false oath of testimony?
outcomeNote: Derived from the absence of ונעלם

segments.he: וְחַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹן הַשְּׁבוּעָה. מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּכוּלָּן נֶאֱמַר בָּהֶן ״וְנֶעְלַם״, וְכָאן לֹא נֶאֱמַר בָּהּ ״וְנֶעְלַם״; לְחַיֵּיב עַל הַמֵּזִיד כַּשּׁוֹגֵג.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And one is liable for» the act of taking a false «oath with intent.» The Gemara asks: «From where is this matter» derived that one is liable to bring a sliding-scale offering for taking a false oath of testimony with intent? It is derived «as the Sages taught: In all of» the other cases where one is liable to bring a sliding-scale offering (see Leviticus 5:2–4), i.e., the defiling of the Temple or its sacrificial foods, and violating an oath on an utterance, «it is stated: “And it is hidden”; but here,» with regard to the oath of testimony, it «is not stated: And it is hidden,» which serves «to render» one «liable» for taking the oath «intentionally» just «as» he is liable for taking the oath «unwittingly.»
